C: Driving a motor vehicle on Idaho’s public highways requires a current driver’s license.
Idaho permits licensing beginning at age fifteen.
Applicants younger than seventeen must finish approved driver training and the graduated licensing program before licensing.
ITD provides reasonable disability accommodations and equal access to its facilities, programs and services.
A skills examiner must administer an equal test regardless of an applicant’s disability.
A person moving to Idaho must apply for an Idaho license within thirty days of establishing residence, even if the prior license remains valid.
An Idaho college or university student may retain a valid other-state license when claiming residency in that other state.
Active-duty military members, their spouses and dependents may retain valid other-state licenses while claiming residence in that state.
An Idaho license applicant must surrender licenses and identification cards issued by another state, a United States territory or the District of Columbia.
A transfer applicant from another state, a United States territory or the District of Columbia must pass Idaho’s Class D knowledge test.
A transfer applicant whose license expired at least twenty-five months earlier must also take the skills test.
Receiving a credential from another jurisdiction cancels the Idaho credential.
A foreign license holder receiving an Idaho Class D license is not required to hand over the foreign license.
After receiving an Idaho Class D license, a driver may not display or use the foreign license as driving authority.
A driver who uses the foreign license after receiving Idaho Class D authority may face a misdemeanor citation and fine.
An applicant seeking disability accommodations should give the county DMV two weeks to arrange them.
An Idaho driver must carry the driver’s license while operating a vehicle.
Misusing or mutilating a license, instruction permit or identification card is a misdemeanor.
A worn, broken or damaged license must be replaced with a duplicate.
Knowingly supplying false information on a credential application can lead to perjury prosecution and cancellation of the credential.
Outstanding license suspensions, cancellations or revocations in another jurisdiction must be cleared before Idaho can issue a license.
County sheriff driver’s license offices issue Idaho licenses, identification cards and instruction permits.
An Idaho credential photograph must show the face fully from the front.
Applicants generally remove face or head coverings for the credential photograph, with possible medical or religious exceptions.
An Idaho Class D license authorizes operation of non-commercial motor vehicles.
A driver training permit lets a person aged fourteen and a half through under seventeen attend an approved public or private driver training program.
During enrollment in driver training, the training permit allows driving only with the training instructor.
Successful driver training completion and return of the permit by the instructor make the applicant eligible to begin supervised instruction.
A parent or guardian with verifiable custody or guardianship must act as liability signer for an applicant younger than eighteen.
A person aged eighteen may apply for a Class D instruction permit without a liability signer.
An applicant aged seventeen or older can use a Class D instruction permit for one year of accompanied driving practice.
The adult accompanying a Class D instruction permit holder must be at least eighteen and hold a valid driver’s license.
Issuance of a Class D instruction permit requires passing the knowledge test.
A driver younger than sixteen is limited to daylight driving unless a licensed driver aged at least twenty-one occupies the adjacent front seat.
For the under-sixteen driving restriction, Idaho defines daylight as five in the morning through ten at night in local time.
C2: During the first six months of licensure, a driver younger than seventeen may carry at most one passenger younger than seventeen unless those passengers are related by blood, adoption or marriage.
A person aged seventeen or older may take driver training using a Class D instruction permit.
A person aged seventeen or older may use a driver training permit or, after driver education, a supervised instruction permit for driver training.
An applicant younger than seventeen who has never held an Idaho license must complete approved driver training and the GDL requirements.
The graduated licensing path requires at least six months of supervised instruction without violations.
The supervising driver during the GDL instruction period must have a valid license and be at least twenty-one.
During GDL supervision, the supervising driver must sit in the front seat next to the learner.
The GDL learner may not carry another passenger in the front seat during supervised instruction.
A GDL learner must ensure that every occupant uses a seat belt or required child restraint.
The supervised GDL period requires compliance with the laws on alcohol and other intoxicating substances.
The GDL learner must log at least fifty hours of supervised driving.
At least ten of the supervised GDL driving hours must occur at night.
A traffic-law conviction during supervised instruction cancels the learner’s permit and requires a new application.
After a traffic-law conviction during supervised instruction, the minimum six-month period begins again when the new permit is issued.
Completion of the GDL requirements must be followed by passing the knowledge and skills tests before a license is issued.
Approved Idaho driver training includes thirty hours of classroom teaching.
Approved Idaho driver training includes six hours observing other students from inside the vehicle.
Approved Idaho driver training includes six hours driving with an approved instructor.
For the younger driver training permit holder, the permit ends five days after the eighteenth birthday.
Idaho drivers seeking an international driving permit must contact AAA because ITD does not issue that permit.
